speaker: Davarn Morrison
captured_statement: The platform already re-evaluates before execution. Full fresh-state reconstruction and evidence binding is an additional high-assurance hardening capability that can be configured where the deployment requires it.

verdict_semantics.ALLOW: The proposed action may remain inside the configured runtime decision envelope; this alone does not prove reconstruction of every materially required commit-time parameter.
verdict_semantics.BLOCK: The proposed action may reach a configured prohibited region; this alone does not prove reconstruction of every materially required commit-time parameter.
verdict_semantics.ERROR: No safe execution permission is created; consequence-binding action should fail closed unless a separately governed fallback is authorized.

unresolved_validation_questions: Can missing materially required evidence be detected rather than treated as unchanged or absent without consequence?
Can contradictory evidence alter an existing ALLOW or BLOCK?
Can late-arriving evidence alter an existing ALLOW or BLOCK before execution?
Can previously unmodeled evidence enter the commit-time decision path?
Can the evaluator detect that relevant evidence was never requested or included?
Does the high-assurance configuration reconstruct current authority, policy, delegation, context, validity, and recoverability as well as evidence?
What latency applies when full fresh-state reconstruction and evidence binding are enabled?
public_claim_limit: The author clarified that ordinary pre-execution re-evaluation and configurable full fresh-state reconstruction/evidence binding are distinct capabilities. No claim is made that every deployment enables the stronger capability or that its behavior has been independently reproduced.
